# Authentic Graph 14 predecessor repositories

These exact repositories and requests were created through the copied accepted named-reference
executable before advancing the validator. Executable SHA-256:
`129a9cd6cb7c2026f365239c88eb7ced2b44ec8db82decefa8497f1b447c787d`;
implemented source `5f49c68d55bdf1f620f1a3ae2fdd462cb02c2847`, startup report
`15c0bfdf82697e1a8dd4df6085e867d4b109bbf7`.

`valid` accepted a simultaneous two-parameter swap and ran to integer 7. `expanding`
accepted `growing<T> -> growing<List<T>>` in an untaken branch; its check/run failed later
with resource diagnostic `reference_instantiation_storage`. Neither program has effects.
The original accepted requests retain their base, idempotency key, and allocated identities.
Catalog and compiler files are retained to distinguish semantic revalidation from catalog repair.

Tests copy these frozen inputs into owned disposable directories. They must never rewrite them
with the successor validator. Detailed command logs and executable copies belong to the campaign's
untracked evidence archive; these small immutable data fixtures are the compatibility inputs.

`dependency/` and `dependency.request` were authored with the same frozen predecessor executable.
They select the expanding supplier without calling it. `supplier-fixed.lkjp` is the predecessor's
exact ordinary body repair to `7`, exported as a complete source container. The current validator
must inspect the old consumer, reject its supplier's complete executable closure, then allow an
ordinary exact dependency replacement through full-candidate repair.

`private-expanding.lkjp` and its literal request were additionally captured with the same frozen
predecessor after implementation began. Its public entry returns 7 without calling the private
generic function; that unused private body creates `FunctionValue< List<T> >` of itself. The old
plan, apply and export passed. The 5,414-byte container has SHA-256
`01efe2a32c3140d9cfaeb0ec9dcc31400120b7147c735ca9ccfabed1025f8605` and transport
`package_transport_f204ee9a82e5a6bb7ff502db3d2254722d80ae09a768412ec39375536a3c2b9f`.
It tests complete supplier body admission independently of the exported interface and runtime reachability.

The two `expanding-*.lkja` files are **adversarial artifacts**, not accepted predecessor delivery.
A temporary, recorded fault suppressed expanding-edge rejection while the ordinary compiler/linker
encoded the expanding canonical body and its corresponding executable. One artifact uses the
untaken direct call; the other retains an unused named function value. No artifact was executed.
The fault and temporary capture test were removed, exact source restored, and the healthy strict
loader rejected both with `kernel_callable_expansion`. Complete enclosing hashes are valid:

| Input | Bytes | SHA-256 |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| expanding-direct.lkja | 9442 | `167416c33810287055dc7117364959b1cdbebe063ad70301352e753f3ffa49e1` |
| expanding-named.lkja | 9909 | `81788d75262419721ce880f8ba383834e4f8f422e552bec25fc878aa54cde5ae` |

The retained fault/capture source and logs belong to the campaign evidence archive. These bytes
test independent admission of producer output; they supply no authority or current validation.
